main_body: A flat brick/paving ground patch (4x3 tiles) with a few blue-grey and grey strips; terrain, not a standing object.
top_band: none - flat ground surface; the repeating light brick rows (L~187) are paving courses, not a top surface
evidence: Terrain kind: a ground patch seen from above with brick-like paving courses. It is not a standing object, so the 3/4 top/front contract does not apply. No side faces and no standing volume. Treated as acceptable ground terrain.

style.evidence: The candidate has 11 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, equal to the paving reference (7) but far below the grass reference (26, 80 colours). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat areas. Mortar and joint lines are neutral dark grey (#565755, 30% neutral edge pixels), a mix of neutral and tinted tones. The brick courses have a repeating pattern with about 4 lightness steps (L 86, 145, 178, 187) and a little speckle on the bricks. It is clean and tileable, with a regular repeating brick rhythm and some blue-grey and grey patches that read as odd strips. It matches the paving reference on tile density and texture but is a little thinner on shading steps than the best Beodeul pieces. A careful artist would likely accept it next to the paving reference.
